fixed.problem: BLOCKING (review of b9433c8): recall described a done task's merge differently from the chat's own '# Your files' facts in the same turn (design §5 rules 9 and 10). There were four errors. (1) A pull request closed without merging read "Its pull request waits for your Merge." (2) A merge the person's Merge left to them, such as after a failed check, said nothing. (3) A merge under way said nothing. (4) A record for an older pull request than the one the task has now read "merged".
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/chat-recall.test.ts 'd1109-chat-recall, run C: CR-2 sessions and tasks' > 'a done task's merge is said as the chat's '# Your files' and the Tasks row say it: merged with its date, closed without merging, waiting for your Merge or merging by itself with the record's sentence; a record of an older pull request says nothing'. At b9433c8 it read 'Add the footer: Accepted · pull request closed. Its pull request waits for your Merge.', and the map task read 'Done. Its pull request merged on 11 Nov.' from a record for its older pull request.
fixed.how: Root cause: recall.ts mergeWords classified the record on its own terms. It returned merged, then waiting_checks, then 'waits for your Merge' for any done task with approval 'none'. It ignored the state, the last outcome, the merge mode and the task's own pull request. Fix: the facts' classification now lives in one exported function, mergeStandOf(record, prUrl, mode), in conversation/project-facts.ts. repositoryFacts uses it and behaves as before (chat-guard.test.ts is unchanged and passes). recall's mergeWords words its result: 'Its pull request was merged on 15 Nov.', '... was closed without merging.', '... waits for your Merge: <the record's sentence>' and '... merges by itself: <the record's sentence>'. A record for another pull request gives nothing. The merged date is left out once a take-out pull request was asked for, because take-out.ts patches the record then, so its updated_at is no longer the merge date (this was a non-blocking review item). The sibling, recall_open's taskText, says the same sentence. The seeds now give the merged and waiting tasks the pull request their record is for: chat-recall.test.ts' seed and recall-home.ts' PULL_REQUESTS. Without that, 'when was the README merged?' dropped out of the golden set while its 0.9 threshold still held (measured recall@3 0.917 without the seed fix, 0.958 with it).
fixed.check_in_the_app: Live check 4 on a repository project. (1) Let a session finish three tasks with pull requests. (2) Press Merge on the Overview for one. (3) Close another's pull request on GitHub and wait a minute for the watcher. (4) Leave the third waiting. The Tasks tab then reads 'Merged', 'Accepted · pull request closed' and 'Accepted · waiting for you to merge'. In the project's Chat ask 'when was the README merged?', 'what happened to the FAQ task?' and 'what happened to the notes task?'. In the model-call log, each recall or recall_open result must say the same as the first call's '# Your files': 'Its pull request was merged on <date>.' with 'Merged: "…"'; 'Its pull request was closed without merging.' with 'Closed without merging: "…"', and never 'waits for your Merge' for that task; 'Its pull request waits for your Merge: <sentence>' with 'Waiting for your Merge: "…"'. The reply must not say the closed one waits for a Merge. Restart Forerunner and ask about the closed one again: same words. Bench walk with the stand-in: /tmp/frbench/fixup-d1109-chat-recall/walk.cjs.

new_problems: Ranking: the person's own earlier question lines can outrank the record they asked about. After the restart, recall {words: 'the FAQ'} ranked the earlier line 'what happened to the FAQ task? (you)' as r1 (strong), ahead of the task 'Write the FAQ' (r2, strong) (/tmp/frbench/fixup-d1109-chat-recall/restart-result.json). A real model can see that r1 is its own question, but a person's earlier question rarely holds an answer. Suggested fix: down-weight the person's conversation lines that are questions (end in '?') in rankRecords, measured against the golden set. Live check 4 should watch which hit the real model opens on a repeated question.

packages/runtime/test/conversation.test.ts 'l3-money-engine, run L3: a chat call its timeout cuts off > a typed turn its timeout cuts off before any token records no time to first token' failed once here, in a parallel run of 7 test files while other agents were busy ('the chat turn had not answered after 60 s of simulated time'). It passed alone 3 times, in two more parallel runs, and in both full pnpm check runs. The fixer saw the same. Its pastTimeout helper gives each simulated second only 8 setImmediate ticks, so any real-time wait before the first model call can let the 60 simulated seconds run out first. That makes it a Windows-CI risk. The test is run L3's.

The fixer's report said the golden set measured recall@3 1.0 and MRR 0.95. At b9433c8 it measures 0.958 and 0.927 (three questions miss r1, one of them lands at r4). The thresholds still hold, and testing.md now gives the measured figures.

tests_changed_for_design.test: packages/runtime/test/chat-recall.test.ts 'CR-2 sessions and tasks' > 'a renamed task is found by its earlier name, with 'Earlier called', and its merge …'
tests_changed_for_design.why: The seed's done tasks now carry the pull request their merge record is for: a real record is always for the task's pull request, and recall, the Tasks row and the facts read a record only for that one. So the status is now the Tasks row's ('Merged', 'Accepted · waiting for you to merge') where it was 'Done', and the merge sentence is the facts' ('Its pull request was merged on 4 Nov.'; 'Its pull request waits for your Merge: #3 waits for you to merge it: press Merge on the Overview.'). task_get's first line reads ': Merged'. The intent is kept: the earlier title, the merge date, and 'waits for your Merge' for the waiting one.

'Write the guide' and 'Write the FAQ' get pull_request URLs (PULL_REQUESTS) when the 3 Nov session finishes them, matching their merge records. Without this the golden question 'when was the README merged?' would not be found, while the 0.9 threshold still held. The thresholds and the questions are unchanged.
